subject: Trial hosting playbook: proposed POC scope & environment options
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Timothy Zhou <tim.zhou@medbridge.com>, Rachel Perez <rachel.perez@medbridge.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-22T15:04:00-07:00
Subject: Trial hosting playbook: proposed POC scope & environment options

Hi Tim / Rachel — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and a proposed POC playbook so we can land scope and environment choice. I outlined three hosting options and a short evaluation plan below. Please review and tell me which option you prefer (hosted / dedicated sandbox / VPC-private) and any blockers on your side.

POC objective (3-week pilot): validate retrieval accuracy on clinical notes + measure end-to-end latency for patient-facing workflows at 95th percentile.

Success criteria (examples):
- Mean MRR > 0.78 on the seeded eval set (we can adapt to your metric)
- 95th percentile inference latency < 350ms for single-request path (demo-friendly threshold)
- No production data stored outside approved environment; audit log visibility for all requests
- Integration completeness: SAML SSO and API key rotation demonstrated

Environment options (tradeoffs):
1) Hosted Redwood API (fastest onboarding) — Pros: immediate start, no infra to provision; Cons: not recommended for PHI unless you accept tokenization/DLP & contract terms.
2) Dedicated sandbox (isolated capacity in Redwood tenancy) — Pros: predictable throughput, faster than VPC; Cons: requires networking allowlist and short provisioning window (3–5 business days).
3) VPC / Private deployment (customer VPC peered or on-prem) — Pros: full data residency and preferred for PHI/regulated data; Cons: longer lead time (2–4 weeks), higher ops coordination.

Evaluation plan and checkpoints:
- Week 0 (this week): confirm environment choice and deliverables (SAML metadata, sample traffic, list of stakeholders).
- Week 1: infra provision + baseline integration (smoke tests).
- Week 2: run seeded evaluation and collect metrics; iterate prompt/temperature.
- Week 3: joint review, handoff plan for expanded pilot (if met success criteria).

Owners / asks:
- Customer: provide SAML metadata, 2 example payloads, security contact, and preferred kickoff window.
- Redwood: Ben Carter (Infra lead) to provision capacity; Marissa Cole (Customer Success) to run eval; Neha Kapoor (Security) to answer compliance questions.

Attachments: redwood-poc-checklist.pdf (checklist + minimally required inputs), networking-diagram.png (draft peering options).

Next steps: please reply with the preferred environment and earliest date for kickoff. If you want an initial demo of the hosted path as a quick spike, we can do that same day.

Thanks,
Priyom Das
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
pri yom.das@redwood.com

From: Timothy Zhou <tim.zhou@medbridge.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Cc: Rachel Perez <rachel.perez@medbridge.com>
Date: 2026-08-23T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Trial hosting playbook: proposed POC scope & environment options

Hi Priyom — thanks for the crisp summary. A few quick clarifications inline: 

- Data residency: the scope will include clinical notes that can contain PHI. We need SOC 2 + written confirmation that PHI will not be permanently stored outside our approved environment.
- Encryption: can you confirm encryption at rest and KMS integration options for the dedicated sandbox and VPC?
- Timeline: we prefer a dedicated sandbox if it meets encryption and audit requirements; VPC would be ideal but might push the pilot too late for our Q3 goals.

If hosted can be used only for anonymized data (and we can run a hosted spike with synthetic data), that might help accelerate some early prompts. Otherwise recommend dedicated sandbox as the default path.

Can your security lead provide a short note on controls and expected time to provision a dedicated sandbox + any networking pre-reqs?

—Tim
Timothy Zhou
Director of Platform Engineering | MedBridge
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Timothy Zhou <tim.zhou@medbridge.com>, Rachel Perez <rachel.perez@medbridge.com>
Date: 2026-08-24T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Trial hosting playbook: proposed POC scope & environment options

Thanks Priyom and Tim — Ben here (Solutions Architect). Short answers + recommended next steps based on PHI requirement: 

Recommendation: start POC on a Dedicated Sandbox with customer-managed KMS (we can support AWS KMS or provide a dedicated key in our tenancy) and strict retention policy. Host a hosted spike with synthetic data if you want to accelerate early prompt tuning.

Tradeoffs and timeline estimates:
- Dedicated sandbox: provisioning and allowlist setup typically 3–5 business days once we have IP ranges and SAML metadata. We provide per-route token auditing and optional KMS integration.
- VPC/private: full peering or on-prem install typically 2–4 weeks (networking approvals + firewall rules + certificate exchange). Good for long-term/regulatory demands but slower.
- Hosted: immediate but only for non-PHI or heavily redacted flows.

Network/security pre-reqs for Dedicated sandbox:
- Customer allowlist: one or two outbound IP ranges (we'll share exact CIDRs).
- SAML metadata + test account for SSO.
- If using customer KMS: an IAM role + key policy we can assume (we'll share steps).

Concrete next actions and owners:
1) Customer: send SAML metadata and preferred inbound IPs (Tim) — due 2026-08-26.
2) Ben (Infra): prepare dedicated sandbox and draft allowlist with estimated CIDRs — ETA 3 business days after items above.
3) Marissa (CS): prepare seeded eval set and coordinate measurement plan — ETA Week 1.
4) Neha (Security): complete short controls note and share SOC2 checklist — ETA 2026-08-25.

I'll attach a rough networking diagram for the dedicated sandbox and a short provisioning checklist (networking-diagram.png). If anyone prefers, we can do a 30-minute technical kickoff next Wednesday (2026-08-28) to walk through allowlist and KMS steps.

Ben Carter
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com
